theorem.statement: For every fixed \(k\in\mathbb N_0\), pointwise numerical edge identification on the literal class \(K_G\le k\) is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete.  Hardness holds already for the restriction of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\) having \(K_G=0\), rational strictly diagonally dominant positive-definite covariance, and a depth-one directed graph of maximum directed outdegree one whose directed weak components are isolated vertices, single directed edges, or three-parent in-stars.  Consequently, if \(N\) denotes total binary input length, an algorithm of bit complexity \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(N)\) for the class posed in the question would imply \(\mathsf P=\forall\mathbb R\).  Thus \(\mathsf{ParamHandle}\), as presently defined, does not yield a fixed-parameter algorithm for that literal class: \(K_G\) does not count vertices of indegree at least three.  The completeness and obstruction hold for exact fibers, including singular fibers, and require no genericity assumption.
theorem.proof_tex:
The fan-in-two completeness theorem supplies a promise-preserving polynomial-time many-one reduction from the \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete complemented planted-selector language to \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\).  Every output of that reduction has rational strictly diagonally dominant positive-definite covariance, and its directed weak components are isolated vertices, single directed edges, or two-parent in-stars; it also has directed depth one and maximum directed outdegree one.

Apply the padding lemma to each output \((G_Q,\Sigma_Q,e_Q)\).  It produces \((\widetilde G_Q,\widetilde\Sigma_Q,e_Q)\) in deterministic polynomial bit complexity, with maximum directed indegree three and \(K_{\widetilde G_Q}=0\), while preserving strict diagonal dominance, positive definiteness, acyclicity, and feasibility.  The exact fiber bijection in that lemma preserves the queried projection, so
\[
\mathcal A_{e_Q}(\widetilde G_Q,\widetilde\Sigma_Q)
=\mathcal A_{e_Q}(G_Q,\Sigma_Q).
\]
By the promise-problem definition, the two triples have the same YES/NO answer because each is a YES instance exactly when its displayed attainable set is a singleton.  Composing the compiler reduction with the padding transformation is therefore a promise-preserving many-one reduction.  The fan-in-two theorem and the equality above prove \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hardness even on the stated subclass with \(K_G=0\).  Notice that this is equality of complete fibers followed by equality of their queried projections; it does not discard poles, singular components, or exceptional solutions.

The published unrestricted numerical edge-identification membership result places the unrestricted promise problem in \(\forall\mathbb R\).  Restricting its promise domain by the polynomial-time decidable conditions \(K_G\le k\) and, for the smaller hard subclass, maximum directed indegree at most three, preserves membership: the same universal real formula decides the singleton-fiber predicate on the restricted promise.  Hence the literal class \(K_G\le k\), and also its maximum-indegree-three restriction, belong to promise \(\forall\mathbb R\).  Since the \(K_G=0\) hard family lies in every class \(K_G\le k\) for \(k\ge0\), each fixed-\(k\) restriction is promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete.

Finally, suppose an exact algorithm had running time \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(N)\), where \(N\) is total encoded bit length.  On the hard subfamily, \(k=0\), so its running time would be the polynomial \(f(0)\operatorname{poly}(N)\).  Together with \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hardness this would place every problem in \(\forall\mathbb R\) in \(\mathsf P\), and the standard inclusion \(\mathsf P\subseteq\forall\mathbb R\) would give \(\mathsf P=\forall\mathbb R\).  The obstruction to using \(\mathsf{ParamHandle}\) is visible directly at \(K_G=0\): it exposes no coefficient belonging to a two-parent vertex, while the padded hard instance retains three-parent vertices and an exactly bijective hard fiber.  This resolves the question in favor of fixed-parameter hardness for the parameter and class as stated.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \((G,\Sigma,e)\) be a triple in the promise domain underlying \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\), and suppose that every directed weak component of \(G\) is an isolated vertex, a single directed edge, or a two-parent in-star.  There is a deterministic polynomial-bit transformation producing \((\widetilde G,\widetilde\Sigma,e)\) such that \(\widetilde G\) is acyclic of depth one, has maximum directed indegree three, maximum directed outdegree one, directed component size at most four, and \(K_{\widetilde G}=0\); moreover, \(\widetilde\Sigma\) is rational and positive definite, and it is strictly diagonally dominant whenever \(\Sigma\) is.  Restriction to the original vertices is a bijection \(\mathcal F_{\widetilde G}(\widetilde\Sigma)\to\mathcal F_G(\Sigma)\), and hence
\[
\mathcal A_e(\widetilde G,\widetilde\Sigma)=\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put
\[
S=\{v\in V:|\operatorname{pa}_D(v)|=2\},\qquad h=|S|,
\]
and introduce pairwise distinct new vertices \(R=\{r_v:v\in S\}\), disjoint from \(V\).  Define
\[
\widetilde V=V\mathbin{\dot\cup}R,
\qquad
\widetilde D=D\cup\{(r_v,v):v\in S\},
\qquad
\widetilde B=B.
\]
Here the last equality regards \(B\) as a set of pairs contained in \(V\), so every pair involving a new vertex is absent from \(\widetilde B\).  Finally, in the vertex order \(V,R\), set
\[
\widetilde\Sigma=
\begin{pmatrix}
\Sigma&0\\
0&I_h
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
These operations append at most \(n\) vertices and entries from \(\{0,1\}\), so they have deterministic polynomial bit complexity in the binary input length.  Rationality is immediate from rationality of \(\Sigma\).  For every nonzero \((a,b)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^h\), positive definiteness of the promised \(\Sigma\) gives
\[
\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\end{pmatrix}^{\!\mathsf T}
\widetilde\Sigma
\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\end{pmatrix}
=a^{\mathsf T}\Sigma a+b^{\mathsf T}b>0.
\]
Thus \(\widetilde\Sigma\succ0\).  If \(\Sigma\) is strictly diagonally dominant, every old row of \(\widetilde\Sigma\) has the same diagonal and off-diagonal absolute row sum as before, while every new row has diagonal one and off-diagonal absolute row sum zero.  Hence strict diagonal dominance is also preserved.

Every supported coefficient matrix on \(\widetilde G\) has a unique block representation
\[
\widetilde L=
\begin{pmatrix}
L&0\\
U&0
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
U_{r_v,j}=
\begin{cases}
u_v,&j=v,\\
0,&j\ne v,
\end{cases}
\]
where \(L\) is supported on \(D\).  Direct block multiplication using the definition of the induced disturbance covariance gives
\[
I_{n+h}-\widetilde L
=
\begin{pmatrix}
I_n-L&0\\
-U&I_h
\end{pmatrix}
\]
and therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Omega_{\widetilde G}(\widetilde L)
&=(I_{n+h}-\widetilde L)^{\mathsf T}
  \widetilde\Sigma
  (I_{n+h}-\widetilde L)\\
&=
\begin{pmatrix}
(I_n-L)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-L)+U^{\mathsf T}U&-U^{\mathsf T}\\
-U&I_h
\end{pmatrix}\\
&=
\begin{pmatrix}
\Omega(L)+U^{\mathsf T}U&-U^{\mathsf T}\\
-U&I_h
\end{pmatrix}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For each \(v\in S\), the pair \(\{r_v,v\}\) is absent from \(\widetilde B\).  The corresponding defining equation of \(\mathcal F_{\widetilde G}(\widetilde\Sigma)\) is, by the lower-left block in the preceding display,
\[
0=[\Omega_{\widetilde G}(\widetilde L)]_{r_v,v}=-U_{r_v,v}=-u_v.
\]
Consequently every point of the enlarged fiber has \(U=0\).  Its old-old disturbance block then equals \(\Omega(L)\), while every off-diagonal entry involving a new vertex is zero.  By the definition of the coefficient fiber, it follows that
\[
\widetilde L\in\mathcal F_{\widetilde G}(\widetilde\Sigma)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
U=0\ \text{ and }\ L\in\mathcal F_G(\Sigma).
\]
Thus restriction \(\widetilde L\mapsto L\) is a bijection, with inverse \(L\mapsto\left(\begin{smallmatrix}L&0\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\).  In particular, nonemptiness of the original promised fiber implies nonemptiness of the enlarged fiber.  The queried edge \(e\) is an old edge and its coefficient is unchanged by both maps; the definition of the attainable set therefore yields
\[
\mathcal A_e(\widetilde G,\widetilde\Sigma)
=\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma).
\]

It remains to verify the graph restrictions.  Each new vertex is a root with one outgoing edge, so adding it cannot create a directed cycle and preserves directed depth one.  Every old vertex of indegree two acquires exactly one new parent and hence has indegree three; vertices of indegree zero or one are unchanged, and new vertices have indegree zero.  Therefore no vertex has indegree exactly two, so \(K_{\widetilde G}=0\), and the maximum indegree is three.  A two-parent in-star becomes a three-parent in-star on four vertices; the other components are unchanged.  Private roots imply maximum directed outdegree one.  This proves all asserted properties without deleting or selecting any branch of the original fiber.

proofs.proof_tex:
We first prove membership.  Write a supported coefficient matrix as a vector
\(\ell=(\ell_{ab})_{(a,b)\in D}\).  Expanding the definition of the fiber gives,
for each unordered pair \(\{i,j\}\notin B\) with \(i\ne j\), the polynomial
\[
 f_{ij}(\ell)
 =\Sigma_{ij}
 -\sum_{a:(a,i)\in D}\ell_{ai}\Sigma_{aj}
 -\sum_{b:(b,j)\in D}\Sigma_{ib}\ell_{bj}
 +\sum_{\substack{a:(a,i)\in D\\ b:(b,j)\in D}}
       \ell_{ai}\Sigma_{ab}\ell_{bj}.
\]
Indeed, this is the \((i,j)\) entry of
\((I_n-L)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-L)\), by direct matrix multiplication.
On the promise in \(\mathrm{def:promise\mbox{-}problem}\), the fiber is nonempty.
Consequently, \(\mathcal A_e(G,\Sigma)\) is a singleton if and only if the
following universal sentence is true:
\[
 \forall \ell\in\mathbb R^{|D|}\ \forall \ell'\in\mathbb R^{|D|},\qquad
 \left[
   \left(\bigwedge_{\substack{i<j\\\{i,j\}\notin B}}f_{ij}(\ell)=0\right)
   \wedge
   \left(\bigwedge_{\substack{i<j\\\{i,j\}\notin B}}f_{ij}(\ell')=0\right)
 \right]
 \Longrightarrow \ell_e=\ell'_e.
\]
The forward implication follows because both queried entries belong to the
singleton attainable set.  Conversely, the displayed sentence makes the
queried-coordinate projection constant on the nonempty fiber, hence makes its
image a singleton by \(\mathrm{def:fiber}\).  There are at most \(n^2\)
quadratic polynomials, their rational coefficients are entries of \(\Sigma\),
and their expanded encoding has polynomial size.  The displayed sentence is
therefore a polynomial-size sentence in the universal theory of the reals.
The conditions that the maximum directed indegree is at most three and that
\(K_G=0\) are decidable directly from the two adjacency matrices in polynomial
time.  Thus the promised restriction in the theorem belongs to
\(\forall\mathbb R\).

We next give the hardness reduction.  Let \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sel}}\),
and apply \(\mathrm{thm:fanin\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}completeness}\) to obtain
\[
 (G_0,\Sigma_0,e_0,\rho_0)=\mathsf C(Q).
\]
The cited theorem gives an acyclic depth-one graph in which every directed
weak component is an isolated vertex, a single edge, or a two-parent in-star;
it also gives a rational, strictly diagonally dominant positive-definite
\(\Sigma_0\), a feasible rational \(\rho_0\), and an exact fiber bijection with
\(\operatorname{Sol}(Q)\).  Let
\[
 S=\{v\in V(G_0):|\operatorname{pa}_{D_0}(v)|=2\}.
\]
For each \(v\in S\), introduce two fresh vertices \(r_v,w_v\), add only the
directed edge \(r_v\to v\), and call its coefficient \(u_v=L_{r_vv}\).  Let
\(G^+=(V^+,D^+,B^+)\), where
\[
 V^+=V(G_0)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{r_v,w_v:v\in S\},
 \qquad
 D^+=D_0\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{(r_v,v):v\in S\},
\]
and
\[
 B^+=B_0\cup
 \left(
   \bigl\{\{x,y\}:x\ne y,\ \{x,y\}\cap(V^+\setminus V(G_0))\ne\varnothing\bigr\}
   \setminus\bigl\{\{v,w_v\}:v\in S\bigr\}
 \right).
\]
Thus the old missing pairs remain missing, and the only new missing pairs are
\(\{v,w_v\}\), one for each \(v\in S\).  In the vertex order consisting of the
old vertices followed by the pairs \((r_v,w_v)\), define
\[
 \Sigma^+
 =\Sigma_0\oplus
   \bigoplus_{v\in S}
   \begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\-1&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This matrix is rational.  It is strictly diagonally dominant because
\(\Sigma_0\) is strictly diagonally dominant and, in each new row, the diagonal
entry is \(2>1\), the sum of the absolute off-diagonal entries.  It is positive
definite because for every nonzero vector written as
\((x_0,(a_v,b_v)_{v\in S})\),
\[
 x_0^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_0x_0
 +\sum_{v\in S}\bigl(2a_v^2-2a_vb_v+2b_v^2\bigr)
 =x_0^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_0x_0
 +\sum_{v\in S}\bigl((a_v-b_v)^2+a_v^2+b_v^2\bigr)>0.
\]
Here the first term is positive whenever \(x_0\ne0\), by the positive
definiteness supplied by \(\mathrm{thm:fanin\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}completeness}\),
and each new summand is positive whenever \((a_v,b_v)\ne(0,0)\).

We now calculate the padded fiber exactly.  For an old missing pair
\(\{i,j\}\notin B_0\), the expansion of \(f_{ij}\) above is unchanged after
padding.  The old block of \(\Sigma^+\) equals \(\Sigma_0\); every term newly
introduced by a parent \(r_v\) contains a covariance between \(r_v\) and an
old vertex, or between \(r_v\) and a new parent belonging to a different
block, and every such covariance is zero.  Hence, for every supported
\(L^+\),
\[
 f^+_{ij}(L^+)=f^0_{ij}(L^+|_{D_0}).
\]
For the new missing pair \(\{v,w_v\}\), the vertex \(w_v\) has no directed
parents, so the same expansion and the block definition of \(\Sigma^+\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 f^+_{v,w_v}(L^+)
 &=\Sigma^+_{v,w_v}
   -\sum_{a\in\operatorname{pa}_{D^+}(v)}L^+_{av}\Sigma^+_{a,w_v}\\
 &=0-L^+_{r_vv}(-1)=u_v.
 \end{aligned}
\]
All old-parent covariances with \(w_v\) vanish.  Since there are no other new
missing pairs, these two identities prove the equivalence
\[
 L^+\in\mathcal F_{G^+}(\Sigma^+)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 L^+|_{D_0}\in\mathcal F_{G_0}(\Sigma_0)
 \ \text{and}\ 
 u_v=0\ \text{for every }v\in S.
\]
It follows equation by equation that restriction to \(D_0\) is a bijection
from the padded fiber to the old fiber, with inverse obtained by adjoining all
\(u_v=0\).  In particular, extending \(\rho_0\) by zeros gives a rational
feasible matrix \(\rho^+\), and, with \(e^+=e_0\),
\[
 \mathcal A_{e^+}(G^+,\Sigma^+)
 =\mathcal A_{e_0}(G_0,\Sigma_0).
\]
No division, rank condition, or exclusion of an algebraic exceptional set was
used in this equivalence, so it preserves all singular branches of the fiber.

The graph \(G^+\) is acyclic: each new directed edge starts at a fresh root and
ends at an old depth-one sink.  Every old vertex of indegree two now has
indegree three, every other old vertex retains indegree zero or one, and each
new vertex has indegree zero.  Therefore
\[
 \max_{v\in V^+}|\operatorname{pa}_{D^+}(v)|\le3,
 \qquad
 K_{G^+}=|\{v:|\operatorname{pa}_{D^+}(v)|=2\}|=0.
\]
The padding adds \(2|S|\) vertices and only the rational entries
\(0,-1,2\); hence it is computable in polynomial time and has polynomial bit
size.

By \(\mathrm{thm:fanin\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}completeness}\), on the source
promise,
\[
 Q\in\mathsf{coSEL\mbox{-}PNQF}
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \mathcal A_{e_0}(G_0,\Sigma_0)=\{0\},
 \qquad
 Q\in\mathsf{SEL\mbox{-}PNQF}
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \mathcal A_{e_0}(G_0,\Sigma_0)=\{0,1\}.
\]
The equality of attainable sets therefore makes the padding a
promise-preserving many-one reduction from the
\(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete complemented source language to the restriction
of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_3\) with \(K_G=0\).  This proves
\(\forall\mathbb R\)-hardness; together with the membership argument, it proves
promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness.

Finally, if the residual-algebra handle in
\(\mathrm{def:parameterized\mbox{-}handle}\) yielded an
\(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(n)\)-time decision algorithm on its stated literal
class, then its restriction to \(k=0\) would run in
\(f(0)\operatorname{poly}(n)\) time on the complete slice just constructed.
Because \(f(0)\) is a fixed constant, this would place a promise
\(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete problem in polynomial time and hence imply
\(\mathsf P=\forall\mathbb R\).  Thus the literal parameter \(K_G\) does not
measure distance from fan-in one: it assigns value zero to the padded
indegree-three hard family.
